title: Pangram AI Detector Cannot Identify Images Rendered by AI-Written Code
summary:
Pangram's latest Image 1.0 software is unable to identify synthetic visuals that are programmatically rendered using code created by AI assistants, such as Claude. The company issued the clarification shortly after moving its image detection tool from research preview to a public release.

The new detector, available via API and a Chrome extension, spots 99.2% of synthetic images with a 0.27% false positive rate. Pangram also introduced a video detection tool that achieved 98.57% accuracy on internal benchmarks. CEO Max Spero said the software uses heatmaps to isolate specific edits, helping users distinguish between fully generated media and the standard AI post-processing used by smartphone cameras.

selectedTweets.text:
We've been working towards AI image and video detection for months, and now it's finally here. 

There were a lot of challenges along the way. There are way more AI image/video models than frontier LLMs, and their outputs are more diverse. Most phone cameras, including iPhones, do some level of AI postprocessing to add detail to real photos.

We had to build a model that's robust to this postprocessing while understanding the difference between AI edits and fully AI-generated visuals. 

I think the heatmap feature is a really important step forward and a huge differentiator over other models which typically report scores as a binary confidence.

Please try it out!!

selectedTweets.text:
This startup just dropped the state-of-the-art AI image and video detection model with 99.9%+ accuracy on both.

AI-generated photos and videos are used to scam people online all the time: for shopping, apartments, dating apps, blackmail and wire fraud. Preventing this is one of the biggest emergent problems of AI.

And it's technically very challenging. Malicious actors blur, noise and add artifacts to circumvent detection. Social apps downscale images. Phones do AI-based post processing too. Catching pointed AI edits in a larger real image is tricky, and you need heatmaps to do it.

AI safety on a frontier model level is important, but what's often neglected is the safety problems AI already poses to the world and Im happy someone's working on it. 

Plus, this is not a "talk to our sales team" or blog post launch. You can go use the API and Chrome extension today!
